text:
Cutter Gauthier is the reason to watch the Ducks right now. He's in the Rocket Richard race alongside Leon Draisaitl, he had a goal streak long enough to make headlines before Scott Wedgewood and the Avalanche shut it down, and he has 16 points in his last ten games. Our numbers say some of that is hot finishing, but he is shooting from good places: we have him at 48% to score tonight, the highest on the slate's two teams.

The problem is everything around him. Anaheim is winless in four (0-4-0), 1-4-0 in five, and banged up: Beckett Sennecke (26 points in 22 games) is on injured reserve until around Nov. 27, Ryan Poehling is out with a knee injury, and Leo Carlsson, hurt in Utah on Saturday, is off the out list and day-to-day. Lukas Dostal has had a hard season, at .857 and 6.8 goals allowed above expected, and he was beaten three times in the third period in Seattle on Monday. The Ducks have taken half the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their last five, so the losing isn't all on the skaters. Our sleeper is Judd Caulfield, a third-liner at 23% to score with six high-danger shots in his last ten games.

San Jose has its own young centre to build around, and Macklin Celebrini has been brilliant against this opponent: 10 points in four career games against Anaheim. Ivar Stenberg, the rookie on his wing, is 54% for a point by our numbers, and Dmitry Orlov has 11 points in ten and is one assist from 300. The Sharks are thin, without Jacob Trouba, Kiefer Sherwood and Igor Chernyshov, and they get outchanced more often than not (45% at five on five). Collin Graf is expected back.

Our numbers have Anaheim at 4.03 expected goals and San Jose at 3.20, the highest total on our board for this pair of shaky defenses. It's the first meeting of the season between two California teams still finding out what they are.
headline: Cutter Gauthier, a winless Ducks team and the Sharks in town
